proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a candidate \(G'\) with \(\overline{G'}=\overline G\).  Work first over the rational-function field \(\mathbb K\) generated by the baseline edge coefficients and the intervention-change coefficients having the exact supports prescribed by \(G\).  Since \(G\) is acyclic, \(\Lambda^{(0)}\) is nilpotent in a topological order, and therefore
\[
 P=(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}
   =I_q+\Lambda^{(0)}+\cdots+(\Lambda^{(0)})^{q-1}.
\]
For \(c,k\in V\), the definition of the actual intervention row gives
\[
 H_{kc}=h_{kc}
 =\sum_{i\in\operatorname{pa}_{G}(k)}\delta_{ki}P_{ic}.
\]
Every entry \(P_{ic}\) is the sum of the weights of all directed baseline paths from \(c\) to \(i\).  Appending the edge \(i\to k^\star\), labelled \(\delta_{ki}\), is a bijection from the terms in the last display to directed paths from \(c\) to the terminal copy \(k^\star\) in \(G^{\mathrm{term}}\).  Thus \(H\) is the path matrix from original vertices to terminal copies.

Let \(C_0\subseteq C\), \(R_0\subseteq R\), and \(|C_0|=|R_0|=m\).  Expand \(\det H[R_0,C_0]\), then expand every entry as its path sum.  If a path family has an intersecting pair, choose the first common original vertex of the lexicographically first such pair and exchange the two tails after that vertex.  The exchange preserves the edge monomial and reverses the endpoint permutation, so it is a sign-reversing involution on intersecting families.  Its survivors are precisely the vertex-disjoint path families.  A surviving edge union determines its constituent paths and endpoint permutation: every selected internal vertex has one selected entering and one selected leaving edge, every source in \(C_0\) begins one path, and every terminal copy in \(R_0^\star\) ends one path.  Hence two distinct surviving families cannot produce the same monomial with opposite signs.  Consequently,
\[
 \det H[R_0,C_0]\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{there are \(m\) vertex-disjoint paths from \(C_0\) to \(R_0^\star\)}.
\]
Taking the largest nonzero minor yields
\[
 \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb K}H[R,C]
 =\max\bigl\{m:\text{there are \(m\) vertex-disjoint paths from \(C\) to \(R^\star\)}\bigr\}.
\]
Vertex splitting with capacity one at every original vertex converts the maximum on the right into an integral maximum-flow problem; a linkage certifies the lower bound and a vertex cut certifies the upper bound.

Every structurally nonzero path minor needed above is included in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{term}}\).  Therefore no such minor vanishes at a point of \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\), while structurally zero minors remain zero under every specialization.  The displayed rank identity consequently holds at every stated parameter point, not merely over \(\mathbb K\).

We next derive the affine conditions.  Write \(U=I_q-\Lambda'^{(0)}\), and for each edge \(j\to i\) of \(G'\) put \(x_{ji}=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{ij}\).  Direct multiplication gives
\[
 (HU)_{kj}=H_{kj}-\sum_{i\in C_j}H_{ki}x_{ji}.
\]
If \(k=j\), then \(H_{jj}=0\), and no child of \(j\) can be an ancestor of \(j\), so the displayed entry is zero.  If \(k\notin\operatorname{de}_{G'}(j)\), same closure implies that neither \(j\) nor a child of \(j\) is an ancestor of \(k\); every term is again zero.  For the remaining nonchildren \(k\in R_j\), the required zero is exactly
\[
 H[R_j,C_j]x_j=H[R_j,j],
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad M_jx_j=b_j.
\]
For a child \(i\in C_j\), the candidate baseline coefficient, the candidate intervention change, and the candidate post-change coefficient are respectively
\[
 x_{ji},\qquad
 (HU)_{ij}=H[i,j]-H[i,C_j]x_j=d_{ji}(x_j),\qquad
 x_{ji}+d_{ji}(x_j).
\]
Thus exact baseline support, exact change support, and edge retention are exactly the three asserted nonvanishing conditions.  No support condition has been omitted: all nonparent entries of \(HU\) are either among the equations indexed by \(R_j\) or are the automatic zeros just proved.

By the batched affine-support lemma, one row reduction of each \((M_j\mid b_j)\) decides feasibility, and the products \(L_jx_j^0+c_j\) and \(L_jN_j\) decide all forbidden forms simultaneously.  If a system is inconsistent or a forbidden form is identically zero, every candidate \(U\) violates a required condition.  If all systems are feasible and no forbidden form vanishes identically, the finite-hyperplane argument in that lemma gives one \(x_j\in\mathcal A_j\) avoiding all forbidden forms for every \(j\).  The column blocks are independent, so these choices assemble into one matrix \(U=I_q-\Lambda'^{(0)}\) with exact support \(G'\), exact intervention-change support, and retained changed edges.  Conversely, any admissible \(U\) provides such a point in every affine block.  This proves the sound-and-complete equivalence with the corrected actual-row class \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\).  The augmented affine-support minors in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{term}}\) make feasibility and identical-vanishing decisions constant on the stated generic locus, so the pointwise test is equivalent to the universal generic quantifier in the definition of that class.

Computing \(P\) and \(H\) costs at most \(O(q^3)\) field operations.  The batched lemma costs \(O(q^4)\) over all columns.  Hence the complete per-candidate test actually satisfies the sharper bound
\[
 O(q^4),
\]
which implies the printed \(O(q^5)\) bound.  An inconsistent reduced row or an identically-zero stacked row is a nonmembership certificate; a linkage or cut certifies each symbolic rank used, and points \(x_j\) avoiding all forbidden forms certify membership.  This is a rational-function field-operation count only; it asserts no expanded bit complexity or coefficient-height bound.

Definition 3.14 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal defines the observational baseline-path class \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G)\); it is not itself being redefined here.  The corrected object is \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\), obtained from the actual rows in their Equation (20).  There are finitely many labelled DAGs on \(V\).  Enumerate the DAGs \(G'\) with closure \(\overline G\), run the actual-row test above, and run the baseline inverse-path rank tests of Definition 3.14.  The two classes agree if and only if the two Boolean outputs agree for every enumerated \(G'\).  This is an exact terminating graph-input procedure; the \(O(q^4)\) bound is per candidate and is not a claim that enumeration is polynomial in \(q\).

The agreement condition cannot be omitted.  Let
\[
 G_\times=\{1\to2,2\to3,3\to4,1\to3\},
 \qquad
 G_{\mathrm{ch}}=\{1\to2,2\to3,3\to4\}.
\]
For the candidate column \(j=1\), put \(\alpha=\Lambda^{(0)}_{21}\), \(b=\Lambda^{(0)}_{32}\), \(c=\Lambda^{(0)}_{43}\), \(d=\Lambda^{(0)}_{31}\), \(\beta=\delta_{32}\), \(\delta=\delta_{31}\), and \(\gamma=\delta_{43}\).  Direct baseline path expansion gives
\[
 P[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 b&d+\alpha b\\
 cb&c(d+\alpha b)
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The second row is \(c\) times the first, and \(b,c\ne0\), so both \(P[\{3,4\},\{2\}]\) and its displayed augmentation have rank one.  For column \(j=2\), the baseline test compares \((P_{43})=(c)\) with \((P_{43},P_{42})=(c,cb)\), both of rank one.  For \(j=3\) and \(j=4\), the nonchild-descendant sets are empty.  Hence every test in Definition 3.14 passes and
\[
 G_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G_\times).
\]
In contrast, direct expansion of the actual rows gives
\[
 H[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 \beta&\delta+\alpha\beta\\
 \gamma b&\gamma(d+\alpha b)
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
and therefore
\[
 \det H[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\gamma(\beta d-b\delta).
\]
This is not the zero polynomial.  For example, \(\alpha=b=c=d=\beta=\gamma=1\), \(\delta=2\), and \(\delta_{21}=1\) give determinant \(-1\).  The post-change coefficients are then \(2\) on \(1\to2\), \(2\) on \(2\to3\), \(3\) on \(1\to3\), and \(2\) on \(3\to4\), so every baseline edge, change, and post-change coefficient is nonzero.  On the relative Zariski-open set where \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\ne0\), the unaugmented actual-row block has rank one and its augmentation has rank two.  Thus its affine system is inconsistent and
\[
 G_{\mathrm{ch}}\notin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_\times).
\]
The resulting nonempty relative Zariski-open exact-change, retained-edge locus satisfies every baseline test and fails the actual-row affine-consistency test.  It refutes the generic equivalence asserted in Theorem 3.15; the correction is to that identification, not to the content of Definition 3.14.

Finally, neither the path, affine, nor agreement calculation uses \(v\) or \(t\).  It remains valid for all positive variances, including \(t_k=v_k\).  The counterexample also lies within the noninjective anchor domain: choose \(p=2<4\) and
\[
 F_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1&1\\0&1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its columns are nonzero and pairwise noncollinear and it has row rank two.  Independently across latent coordinates, take standardized Rademacher errors in the baseline context and, at each target context, replace the target coordinate by a centered unit-variance Laplace error while retaining independent non-Gaussian laws for the other coordinates.  The target standardized fourth cumulant changes from \(-2\) to \(3\).  Scaling these laws realizes any prescribed positive variances without changing the standardized cumulants.  Hence independence, centering, non-Gaussianity, positivity, and unequal scaled cumulants can be imposed without altering the coefficient determinant.  The exact-change retained-edge counterexample locus is therefore contained in the generic soft-intervention domain of Assumption 1.2 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal after this choice of source laws.  A counterexample on a subclass refutes a universal assertion on its superclass; conversely, a positive result proved only on the subclass does not transfer upward without a separate extension argument.

added_lemmas.statement: For the affine blocks associated with a fixed candidate DAG \(G'\), feasibility of all \(q\) systems \(M_jx_j=b_j\) and identical-vanishing of all \(3|C_j|\) forbidden forms \(x_{ji}\), \(d_{ji}(x_j)\), and \(x_{ji}+d_{ji}(x_j)\) can be decided over any infinite coefficient field by row-reducing each augmented matrix \((M_j\mid b_j)\) once.  If a block is feasible, extracting one particular solution and one kernel basis and then performing two batched matrix products decides every forbidden form.  Over all columns this uses \(O(q^4)\) field operations and yields either an inconsistency or identically-zero-form certificate, or a point in every \(\mathcal A_j\) avoiding every forbidden hyperplane.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(n_j=|C_j|\), \(r_j=|R_j|\), and \(B_j=(M_j\mid b_j)\).  Gaussian elimination on \(B_j\) decides
\[
 \operatorname{rank}M_j=\operatorname{rank}B_j.
\]
If the ranks differ, a row of the reduced augmented matrix of the form \((0,\ldots,0\mid 1)\), after rescaling, certifies inconsistency.  Suppose that the ranks agree.  The same reduction, with no second elimination, returns a particular solution \(x_j^0\) and a matrix \(N_j\) whose columns form a basis of \(\ker M_j\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal A_j=x_j^0+\operatorname{im}N_j.
\]

Stack the forbidden affine forms in the order
\[
 \bigl(x_{ji},\ d_{ji}(x_j),\ x_{ji}+d_{ji}(x_j)\bigr)_{i\in C_j}
 =L_jx_j+c_j,
\]
where the three rows corresponding to \(i\in C_j\) have linear parts
\[
 e_i^{\mathsf T},\qquad -H[i,C_j],\qquad e_i^{\mathsf T}-H[i,C_j]
\]
and respective constants
\[
 0,\qquad H[i,j],\qquad H[i,j].
\]
For a row \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}x+c\) of this stack and an arbitrary point \(x=x_j^0+N_jy\) of \(\mathcal A_j\),
\[
 \lambda^{\mathsf T}x+c
 =\lambda^{\mathsf T}x_j^0+c+\lambda^{\mathsf T}N_jy.
\]
It follows directly that this form vanishes identically on \(\mathcal A_j\) if and only if its entry in \(L_jx_j^0+c_j\) is zero and its entire row in \(L_jN_j\) is zero.  Thus the two displayed batched products decide all \(3n_j\) forms.

If no forbidden form is identically zero, each of its zero sets is a proper affine hyperplane of \(\mathcal A_j\).  Their finite union cannot cover \(\mathcal A_j\) over an infinite field.  Indeed, choose affine coordinates \(y\) on \(\mathcal A_j\), choose a direction successively outside the finitely many kernels of the nonconstant forms, and then choose the scalar coordinate outside the finitely many resulting roots; constant nonzero forms have no roots.  The resulting point avoids every forbidden hyperplane.  Conversely, any point avoiding the forbidden forms certifies feasibility and proves that no one of them vanishes identically.

The matrix \(B_j\) has at most \(q\) rows and \(q+1\) columns, so its reduction costs \(O(q^3)\) field operations.  The matrices \(L_j\), \(N_j\) have sizes at most \(3q\times q\) and \(q\times q\), respectively; constructing the stack and computing \(L_jx_j^0+c_j\) and \(L_jN_j\) also costs \(O(q^3)\).  Summing over \(j\in V\) gives \(O(q^4)\).  This counts arithmetic in the coefficient field and makes no expanded bit-complexity or coefficient-height claim.

added_lemmas.statement: For \(p=2<q=4\), the relative Zariski-open exact-change and retained-edge counterexample locus exhibited by the published-mismatch proposition can be equipped with a full-row-rank mixing matrix having nonzero pairwise noncollinear columns and with independent centered non-Gaussian source laws whose target standardized fourth cumulants differ between baseline and target contexts.  It is therefore contained in the generic soft-intervention domain of Assumption 1.2 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal.  Consequently the subclass counterexample refutes the universal identification in their Theorem 3.15 on the superclass, whereas a positive result proved only for the exact-change retained-edge subclass does not by inclusion alone extend to that superclass.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The published-mismatch proposition supplies a nonempty relative Zariski-open coefficient locus on which all required baseline coefficients, all incoming-edge changes, and all post-change coefficients are nonzero, while \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G_\times)\) and \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\notin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_\times)\).  The determinant producing this separation depends only on \(\Lambda^{(0)}\) and \(\delta\), so mixing matrices and error laws may be selected independently of it.

Take
\[
 F_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1&1\\0&1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The determinants of its six pairs of columns are \(1,1,2,-1,-1,1\).  Hence every column is nonzero, every two columns are noncollinear, and \(\operatorname{rank}F_0=2\).  Let \(R\) be a Rademacher random variable, and let \(L\) be a centered Laplace random variable scaled to have variance one.  Both are centered and non-Gaussian.  Their standardized fourth cumulants are, respectively,
\[
 \mathbb E[R^4]-3=-2,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[L^4]-3=3.
\]
In the baseline context choose mutually independent copies of \(R\) for the four errors.  In target context \(k\), choose a copy of \(L\) for error \(k\) and mutually independent copies of \(R\) for the remaining errors.  Multiplication by the positive square roots of the desired variances preserves centering, independence, non-Gaussianity, and standardized fourth cumulants while producing the required positive diagonal covariance matrices.  Thus every target has unequal baseline and intervention scaled fourth cumulants.

These choices meet the mixing and source-law clauses without changing the coefficient point or its nonzero determinant.  Together with the exact-change and retained-edge properties already proved, they place the counterexample inside the stated generic soft-intervention domain.  If \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal B\), a point of \(\mathcal A\) violating a universally quantified assertion on \(\mathcal B\) refutes that assertion.  In the reverse direction, validity on \(\mathcal A\) alone gives no value on \(\mathcal B\setminus\mathcal A\).  Applying these elementary inclusion implications proves the two transfer claims.

added_lemmas.statement: The sound-and-complete membership and nonmembership algorithm of the terminal-certificate theorem can be implemented in \(O(q^4)\) rational-function field operations per same-closure candidate \(G'\): row-reduce each augmented block \((M_j\mid b_j)\) once, extract one particular solution and one kernel basis, stack all \(3|C_j|\) forbidden affine forms, and evaluate their values and kernel restrictions in two batched matrix products.  This is an arithmetic-field bound and is not an expanded bit-complexity or coefficient-height bound.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: The terminal-certificate theorem reduces candidate membership exactly to feasibility of the \(q\) affine systems and non-identical-vanishing of their forbidden forms.  Computing \(P=(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) and \(H\) takes \(O(q^3)\) field operations.  The batched affine-support lemma performs one elimination and two batched products for each column in \(O(q^3)\) operations, hence \(O(q^4)\) over all \(q\) columns.  The linkage or cut part is combinatorial and introduces no rational-function field operations.  Adding the costs proves the claimed \(O(q^4)\) bound.  The same lemma supplies the inconsistency, identical-form, or avoiding-point certificates, and the terminal-certificate theorem proves their soundness and completeness.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(T>0\) with \(T\ne1\), let \(\mathcal R\) and \(\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\) be the aligned factorization datum and the five covariance matrices generated by the true member of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\).  Then, modulo the common monomial action \(\mathfrak M_q\),
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}\bigl(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\bigr)
 \setminus
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R).
\]
This is a pointwise observable separation.  It neither proves that the union of the eight legal positive-real fork branches is dense in every full-dimensional true chamber nor proves \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in\mathsf{Frontier}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), and take the observable datum generated by the true point of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\).  The fork rational-collision proposition constructs a legal parameter point for \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\) with positive baseline and intervention variances, full-row-rank mixing, nonzero pairwise noncollinear mixing columns, exact nonzero graph and change supports, retained changed edges, and
\[
 \Sigma^{(k)}_{\mathrm{candidate}}
 =\Sigma^{(k)}_{\mathrm{true}}
 \qquad(k\in K).
\]
The two fork graphs have the same transitive closure.  By the definition of the pointwise covariance graph set, this legal candidate realization proves
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}\bigl(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\bigr).
\]

It remains to exclude the candidate from the pointwise soft graph set; covariance equality alone does not do so.  Suppose for contradiction that \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)\).  The observable-quotient proposition permits a common permutation and nonzero diagonal rescaling, followed by the rational projective gauge, without changing pointwise membership.  We may therefore align the candidate labels and loading scales with the true representative.  In that representative the rank-one context updates recover the true actual intervention rows.  From the fork witness,
\[
 h_3^{\mathsf T}=(3,1,0,0),
 \qquad
 h_4^{\mathsf T}=(1,1,0,0).
\]
For the candidate graph \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\), column \(j=1\) has \(C_1=\{2\}\) and \(R_1=\{3,4\}\).  If \(x=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{21}\), exact zero support of the candidate change rows at the nonchild descendants requires
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}H_{32}\\H_{42}\end{pmatrix}x
 =\begin{pmatrix}H_{31}\\H_{41}\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad\text{that is,}\qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}x
 =\begin{pmatrix}3\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This system is inconsistent because its augmented determinant is
\[
 \det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\1&1\end{pmatrix}=-2.
\]
Thus no parameter point for \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\) can generate the supplied aligned factorization datum, contradicting pointwise soft membership.  Hence
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\notin\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R).
\]
The observable-quotient proposition transports both the covariance witness and this affine inconsistency through every representative of the common monomial orbit, proving the quotient-valued difference assertion.

Finally, the same proposition distinguishes pointwise membership from the chamberwise definitions.  The rational-collision family supplies one point for every admissible \(T\), while \(\mathsf{Cov}_2\) requires density of the complete legal branch union in every full-dimensional chamber.  Neither the collision nor the determinant \(-2\) proves that density.  Therefore no chamberwise-density or \(\mathsf{Frontier}_2\)-membership conclusion follows.

proposed.statement: For every \(G'\) with \(\overline{G'}=\overline G\) and every \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\), \(G'\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) if and only if, for every \(j\in V\), the affine space \(\mathcal A_j\) is nonempty and none of \(x_{ji}\), \(d_{ji}(x_j)\), or \(x_{ji}+d_{ji}(x_j)\), for \(i\in C_j\), vanishes identically on \(\mathcal A_j\). For all \(R,C\subseteq V\), \(\operatorname{rank}H[R,C]\) equals the maximum number of vertex-disjoint paths from \(C\) to terminal copies \(R^{\star}\) in \(G^{\mathrm{term}}\). These conditions give sound and complete membership and nonmembership certificates in \(O(q^5)\) rational-function field operations. The baseline-path class in Definition 3.14 agrees with corrected actual-row compatibility exactly when these tests agree with its baseline inverse-path rank tests for every same-closure candidate \(G'\); this is an exact finite graph-input decision procedure, and the four-node counterexample below proves that the equivalence asserted by Theorem 3.15 is false without this agreement condition. This structural result holds throughout the positive-variance ambient model, including \(t_k=v_k\).
proposed.justification: This is the corrected sound-and-complete combinatorial answer to actual-row compatibility, with a sharper batched field-operation bound.
proposed.gap: Equation (20) of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal uses the actual inverse-update rows, whereas the proof of their Theorem 3.15 specializes independent changes to baseline coefficients when connecting to Definition 3.14. Terminal-copy linkage and affine nonvanishing repair that step without redefining Definition 3.14.
proposed.consumer: This returns the corrected compatible DAG set with auditable linkage, affine inconsistency, and support certificates for the companion LCD workflow.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The published baseline-path class is now an explicit dependency, and the batched affine-support lemma records the sharper \(O(q^4)\) algorithm used by the proof.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R),\;\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\setminus\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)\bigr)\) modulo the common monomial action \(\mathfrak M_q\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The proved headline is the corrected observable soft graph set together with a quotient-invariant pointwise covariance separation, not the unresolved chamberwise frontier.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\bigl(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\bigr)\longmapsto\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R),\;\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\setminus\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)\bigr)/\mathfrak M_q\), with the soft set evaluated by actual-row terminal and affine certificates and covariance membership evaluated pointwise by a legal positive-real realization.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The functional must name the pointwise observable input and its accepted sign, scale, and permutation quotient rather than advertise unresolved chamberwise density.

proposed.comparator_claim: Equation (20) derives compatibility from the actual \(\Delta^{(k)}_{k,\cdot}\) rows, Definition 3.14 defines baseline inverse-path compatibility, and Theorem 3.15 identifies the two generic rank tests.
Theorem 1.7 gives the paper's recovery anchor, while Problems 5.1--5.2 ask for compatible graphs and whether higher-cumulant compatibility is strictly smaller than covariance compatibility.
proposed.matched_by: Fork pointwise-separation corollary only; chamberwise strictness remains open

proposed.comparator_claim: The injective soft-intervention model recovers transitive-closure information; it does not decide the noninjective positive-real covariance projection.
proposed.matched_by: Observable quotient proposition uses aligned population input rather than extending the injective theorem

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper treats unpaired observational and interventional data under generalized faithfulness and recovers an equivalence class.
Theorem 2.8 characterizes generic covariance-submatrix rank by trek separation.
The half-trek criterion supplies a polynomial-time sufficient certificate for generic rational identifiability.
The paper studies half-trek criteria for identifiability of latent-variable models.
Sections IV--V provide semidefinite tests and positive-semidefinite decomposition and realization machinery for latent causal structures.
Theorems 3.10--3.11 study semialgebraic images under affine-birational parametrizations and saturated vanishing ideals.
The paper accelerates real elimination by dynamic programming over a primal graph of co-occurring variables.

prose_updates.tldr: The headline is now exact and pointwise. Actual soft-intervention rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) admit a sound-and-complete terminal-copy linkage and batched affine-support test in \(O(q^4)\) rational-function field operations. Definition 3.14 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal remains the published baseline-path class; the four-node determinant \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\) shows that Theorem 3.15 incorrectly identifies it with actual-row compatibility. For every \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), the worked \(p=2,q=4\) fork datum has a quotient-invariant pointwise covariance realization by \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\) but the actual-row obstruction \(-2\) excludes that graph from the pointwise soft set. This does not prove chamberwise density or \(\mathsf{Frontier}_2\) membership. The all-branch positive-real compiler remains open.

project_justification.gap: Equation (20) of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal uses the actual inverse-update rows, while Definition 3.14 deliberately records a baseline inverse-path class. The gap is in Theorem 3.15's identification of those two rank systems: specializing independent intervention changes to baseline coefficients can lower an augmented rank. Problem 5.2 poses a separate covariance-versus-higher-cumulant question, but neither the fork chamberwise density alternative nor a graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination criterion is established.
project_justification.niche: The contribution separates three levels that had been conflated: exact actual-row graph compatibility, quotient-invariant pointwise observable covariance separation, and robust chamberwise covariance density. Terminal-copy linkage plus one batched affine reduction per candidate column completely solves the first. The rational fork family and its \(-2\) affine inconsistency solve a concrete pointwise instance of the second. The third remains an explicitly delimited projection problem.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers the corrected \(O(q^4)\) terminal algorithm, an exact finite comparison with the unchanged Definition 3.14 class, an anchor-domain counterexample to Theorem 3.15, and the pointwise fork covariance-minus-soft graph witness modulo common sign, scale, and permutation action. Covariance factor branches and the eight-system fork reduction remain secondary diagnostics. No chamberwise dense cover, full-dimensional separator, all-pair compiler, pathwidth guarantee, coefficient-height bound, or infinite generic-strictness family is claimed.

sampling_model.design: Population structure identification from one baseline and one unknown-target single-node soft-intervention context per latent node. The terminal actual-row theorem covers \(2\le p\le q\); the pointwise covariance separation is the worked noninjective case \(p=2,q=4\).
sampling_model.units: Inputs are the aligned population factorization datum \(\mathcal R\) and, for pointwise covariance comparison, the \(q+1\) population covariance matrices \(\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\). There is no finite-sample claim.
sampling_model.treatment: Each non-source context changes every incoming coefficient of one latent target and retains every changed edge. Graphs and certificates are identified only modulo one common latent permutation and nonzero diagonal scaling.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition applies. All error variances are positive. Terminal compatibility also permits \(t_k=v_k\); the worked fork pointwise family assumes \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\). Chamberwise covariance claims, where discussed diagnostically, retain both signs of true variance change and permit variance-neutral candidate twins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Aligned factor directions and source laws modulo common monomial action are population inputs. Recovery from raw laws, finite-sample cumulant estimation, and uniform statistical error control are outside scope.

prose_updates.related_work: Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) provide the recovery anchor in Theorem 1.7, derive the actual intervention-row equations in Equation (20), define the baseline inverse-path class in Definition 3.14, identify those systems in Theorem 3.15, and pose compatible-graph and covariance-versus-higher-cumulant questions in Problems 5.1--5.2. The present correction preserves Definition 3.14 and refutes only the unsupported identification in Theorem 3.15. Squires, Seigal, Bhate, and Uhler (2023) recover transitive-closure information for injective soft-intervention models; that result does not decide the noninjective positive-real projection here. Half-trek, semidefinite realization, affine-birational, and tree-accelerated elimination results remain methodological context rather than claimed solutions to the open branch-union problem.
prose_updates.interpretation: At population level the companion LCD workflow can now return the corrected actual-row compatible DAG set and, for each accepted or rejected candidate, a terminal linkage or cut, an affine inconsistency, an identically-zero support form, or an avoiding-point certificate. For the worked fork datum it can additionally report a genuine pointwise covariance alternative: the candidate reproduces all five covariances but cannot reproduce the aligned soft-intervention factor datum, and this verdict is invariant to sign, scale, and permutation representatives. It must label that conclusion pointwise. Higher cumulants remove this displayed covariance alternative, but whether they remove covariance alternatives generically across each full-dimensional chamber remains unresolved.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The complete regular fork fiber is reduced to eight legal two-scalar positive systems, but their projected union has not been classified over the full true parameter domain. The prescribed fixed resultant and subresultant attempt retained all true coordinates as parameters and eliminated only the two candidate scalars; it failed before emitting projection polynomials, sign cells, or Thom-encoded sample certificates. The rational \(T\)-family, positive candidate variances \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\), exact five-covariance verification, the obstruction \(-2\), and audited Jacobian regularity establish pointwise feasibility and local facts only. They cannot certify chamberwise density or a full-dimensional separator.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The corrected terminal theorem is exact on its declared generic coefficient locus, independent of variance activity, and has an \(O(q^4)\) arithmetic-field bound with no expanded bit-complexity claim. Its finite Definition 3.14 agreement procedure may enumerate same-closure DAGs, so no polynomial total graph-enumeration bound is asserted. The anchor transfer is one-way: the exact-change retained-edge counterexample lies inside the published generic soft domain and therefore refutes a superclass theorem, while positive subclass results do not automatically extend upward. The fork corollary is quotient-invariant and pointwise; it explicitly does not establish \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in\mathsf{Frontier}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\). The all-chamber fork density test, dense-cover or separator certificates, all-pair non-quantifier-elimination compiler, complexity and pathwidth bounds, and infinite equality or generic-strictness families remain open.
